content: 1. Clofazimine and ceritinib both prolong the QTc interval, which can increase the risk of life-threatening arrhythmias such as Torsades de Pointes. Their coadministration is contraindicated due to this significant risk. 2. Clofazimine and clarithromycin also prolong the QTc interval, and their combined use is contraindicated for the same reasons. 3. Adagrasib and clofazimine each enhance the QTc-prolonging effects of the other. This combination should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. If coadministration is unavoidable, frequent ECG monitoring is recommended to mitigate the risk of Torsades de Pointes and other serious arrhythmias. 4. Clofazimine and entrectinib both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative therapies. If unavoidable, monitor the patient closely with ECGs. 5. Fexinidazole and clofazimine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combined use or select alternative treatments. Fexinidazole should not be coadministered with drugs that block potassium channels or further prolong the QT interval. 6. Clofazimine and givinostat both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is necessary, obtain ECGs at baseline, during treatment, and as clinically indicated. Discontinue treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or increases by more than 60 ms from baseline. 7. Clofazimine and glasdegib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combined use or select alternative therapies. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for an increased risk of QTc prolongation. 8. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and clofazimine both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 9. Ivosidenib and clofazimine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combined use or replace with alternative therapies. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for QTc prolongation and associated risks. 10. Lefamulin and clofazimine both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 11. Macimorelin and clofazimine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid their combined use or use alternative therapies. Macimorelin increases the QTc interval by approximately 11 ms. Allow sufficient washout time for QT-prolonging drugs before initiating macimorelin. 12. Mavorixafor and clofazimine both increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Mavorixafor causes concentration-dependent QTc prolongation. Monitor QTc during treatment, especially in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation. Dose reduction or discontinuation may be required. 13. Mirtazapine and clofazimine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Osilodrostat and clofazimine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Oxaliplatin increases the levels or effects of clofazimine. Use caution and monitor for ECG changes if therapy is initiated in patients taking QT-prolonging drugs. 16. Ozanimod and clofazimine both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Treatment with ozanimod should generally not be initiated in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties. 17. Clofazimine and pitolisant both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 18. Quizartinib and clofazimine both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Monitor patients more frequently with ECGs if coadministered with QT-prolonging drugs. 19. Ribociclib and clofazimine both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 20. Clofazimine decreases the levels of rifampin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 21. Selpercatinib increases the toxicity of clofazimine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Clofazimine decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration with antibiotics decreases efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. 23. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride increases the toxicity of clofazimine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider preand post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at increased risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 24. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate increases the toxicity of clofazimine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider preand post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at increased risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 25. Triclabendazole and clofazimine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Voclosporin and clofazimine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Clofazimine is associated with a high incidence of skin discoloration (75–100%). Gastrointestinal side effects include abdominal and epigastric pain, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, and GI intolerance (40–50%). Dermatologic effects include ichthyosis, dry skin (8–28%), rash, and pruritus (1–5%). Ocular effects include conjunctival and corneal pigmentation due to crystal deposits, dryness, burning, itching, and irritation (>1%). Discoloration of urine, feces, sputum, and sweat (>1%) has also been reported. Other effects include increased blood glucose levels (>1%), elevated ESR (>1%), phototoxicity, erythroderma, acneiform eruptions, and monilial cheilosis.
